The combined account balances held on deposit at each institution typically exceed Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) insurance coverage and, as a result, there is a concentration of credit risk related to amounts on deposit in excess of FDIC insurance coverage. The Company seeks to reduce this risk by maintaining such deposits with high quality financial institutions that management believes are creditworthy. Further, the Company seeks</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">to minimize its exposure to banking risk by limiting the amount of uninsured deposits and investing its excess cash in U.S. government securities, and money market funds.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Company invests excess cash primarily in U.S. treasury bills and money market funds.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The Company classifies all marketable securities that have stated maturities of three months or less from the date of purchase as cash equivalents, and those that have stated maturities of over three months but one year or less as short-term investments on the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets. The Company determines the appropriate classification of investments in marketable securities at the time of purchase and reevaluates such designation at each balance sheet date. Marketable securities that are held for resale are classified as "trading securities" and are measured at fair value with the related gains and losses, including unrealized, recognized in interest expense, net. Marketable securities not classified as held to maturity or as trading securities are classified as "available-for-sale securities" and the fair value option (&#8220;FVO&#8221;) was elected, for which related gains and losses, including unrealized gains and losses and interest, are recognized in interest expense, net. The FVO election allows the Company to account for the marketable securities at fair value, which is consistent with the manner in which the instruments are managed. font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Basic loss per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) excludes dilution for common stock equivalents and is computed by dividing net loss available to stockholders by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding for the period. Restricted shares are included in the computation of basic EPS as they vest.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Diluted EPS is computed using the weighted average number of shares and diluted potential shares outstanding to the extent the effect would not be antidilutive. </span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Dilutive potential shares of common stock are additional shares of common stock assumed to be exercised determined using the treasury stock method or if-converted method. Adjustments to the numerator are made for diluted EPS, including reversal of mark-to-market (&#8220;MTM&#8221;) adjustments recognized in earnings related to private placement warrants and derivative liability, to the extent the combined effect of the numerator and denominator adjustments is dilutive.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_c53f88b4b3cdbe400898'"><ix:exclude><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; z-index: 100;">8</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></ix:exclude></div></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation></div></div><div class="Section_12"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'1bd-2e8-812-21f-79d2'"><ix:continuation id="c26b0f4e4c3856bcaebf" continuedAt="c805915871757dcca1a8"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'ccf94ab88a74ced0c4f9'"><ix:continuation id="ce8c4fb17c43818622aa"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cea93ef4909fd7b810ec'; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'a9b-00a-001-1ca-1baa'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentsPolicy" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag652"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:10.8pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Equity Method Investment</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:10.8pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-family:'Segoe UI'; font-size:9pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:10.8pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The Company applies the equity method of accounting to investments when it has significant influence, but not controlling interest, in the investee. Judgment regarding the level of influence over each equity method investment includes considering key factors such as ownership interest, representation on the board of directors, participation in policy-making decisions and material intercompany transactions. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:10.8pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-family:'Segoe UI'; font-size:9pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The initial carrying value of equity method investment is based on the amount paid to purchase the interest in the investee entity. Subsequently, the investment is increased or decreased by the Company&#8217;s proportionate share in the investee&#8217;s earnings or losses and decreased by cash distributions from the investee. The Company eliminates from its financial results all significant intercompany transactions to the extent of its ownership interest, including the intercompany portion of transactions with equity method investee. The Company&#8217;s share of the investee&#8217;s income or loss is recorded on a one quarter lag.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The Company evaluates equity method investment for impairment based upon a comparison of the fair value of the equity method investment to its carrying value, when impairment indicators exist. If the Company determines a decline in the fair value of an equity method investment below its carrying value is other-than-temporary, an impairment is recorded. Determining fair value involves significant judgment. The Company&#8217;s estimates consider alternative evidence including, but not limited to, general economic conditions and other relevant factors. The Company did not recognize any impairment losses for its equity method investment for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and for the year ended December 31, 2025.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cdb989905848bc0cf3dc'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag636" continuedAt="c0c5f353c41b366a878c"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Leases</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">NextNav leases office spaces under non-cancellable leases as well as site leases for towers and shelters under operating leases related to its network. Site leases are entered into throughout the United States under which NextNav receives the rights to install equipment used to transmit its services over its licensed spectrum. The Company, at the inception of the contract, determines whether a contract is or contains a lease based on assessment of the terms and conditions of the contract. The Company classifies leases with contractual terms longer than twelve months as either operating or finance. The Company has elected not to recognize lease assets and liabilities for its short-term leases, which are defined as leases with an initial term of twelve months or less. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_cc6b406968ca727873a5'"><ix:exclude><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; z-index: 100;">9</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></ix:exclude></div></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation></div></div><div class="Section_13"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'1bd-2e8-812-21f-79d2'"><ix:continuation id="c805915871757dcca1a8" continuedAt="c4f3105125d63dc51d72"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cdb989905848bc0cf3dc'"><ix:continuation id="c0c5f353c41b366a878c"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The Company&#8217;s leases may include options to extend or terminate the lease. The option to renew may be automatic, at the option of NextNav or mutually agreed to between the landlord and NextNav. Lease terms include the non-cancellable term and periods under options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise that option.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The Company&#8217;s lease agreements generally contain lease and non-lease components. Payments under the lease arrangements are primarily fixed. Non-lease components primarily include payments for utilities and maintenance. The Company combines fixed payments for non-lease components with lease payments and accounts for them together as a single lease component which increases the amount of the Company&#8217;s lease assets and liabilities. Certain lease agreements contain variable payments, which are expensed as incurred and not included in the lease assets and liabilities. These amounts include payments for common area maintenance.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Lease assets and liabilities are recognized at the present value of the future lease payments at the lease commencement date. The interest rate used to determine the present value of the future lease payments is the Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate, because the interest rate implicit in the Company&#8217;s leases is not readily determinable. The Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate is estimated to approximate the interest rate on a collateralized basis with similar terms and payments, and in economic environments where the leased asset is located. Lease assets are reduced by landlord incentives, plus any direct costs from executing the leases or lease prepayments reclassified from &#8220;Other current assets&#8221; upon lease commencement.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Operating lease expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Monthly rent expense includes any site related utility payments or other fees such as administrative or up-front fees contained in the lease agreements that are determinable upon execution of the lease agreement.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p></ix:continuation></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'d37-266-cef-438-b203'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag643"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Property and Equipment and Network under Construction </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Property and equipment, net of accumulated depreciation and network under construction are recorded at cost. Employee-related costs for construction of network assets are also capitalized during the construction phase. Expenditures for maintenance and repairs that do not materially extend the useful lives of property and equipment are charged to cost of goods sold (&#8220;COGS&#8221;) and selling, general and administrative as incurred. When property or equipment is retired or otherwise disposed of, the related property accounts are relieved of costs and accumulated depreciation and any resulting gain or loss is included in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><br/><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Acquired finite-lived intangible assets primarily includes proprietary technology and software.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">See Note 4 &#8212; Intangibles.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'1ae-c04-341-035-f4ec'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsIntangibleAssetsIndefiniteLivedPolicy" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag644" continuedAt="c7b7de706d59ca1b592c"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Indefinite-Lived Intangible assets</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold;; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">NextNav holds wireless Multilateration Location and Monitoring Service (&#8220;LMS&#8221;) licenses. Certain general regulatory requirements apply to some of the licensed wireless spectrum held by NextNav, including, for example, certain build-out or &#8220;substantial service&#8221; requirements, which generally must be satisfied as a condition to the license. NextNav is actively engaged in either meeting such requirements currently or seeking an extension of such requirements from the Federal Communications Commission (&#8220;FCC&#8221;) for each of its LMS licenses subjected to the requirements. Although licenses are issued by the FCC for only a fixed time,</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'9bc-448-db2-cf2-ebdf'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt"><ix:nonNumeric name="nn:IndefiniteLivedLicenseAgreementsWithFederalGovernmentTerm" contextRef="D20260331" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" id="Tag472">ten&#160;years</ix:nonNumeric></span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, such licenses are subject to renewal by the FCC, based on the achievement of certain milestones and a finding that such renewal would serve the public interest. Upon renewal, the licenses are granted for additional</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Tag691;-aw-sdt-tag:'6df-8f4-07f-785-940a'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">ten-year</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">periods. Renewal of NextNav&#8217;s licenses has occurred previously and at nominal cost. As a result, NextNav treats its wireless LMS spectrum licenses as an indefinite-lived intangible asset. NextNav reevaluates the useful life determination for wireless licenses each year to determine whether events and circumstances continue to support an indefinite useful life. Costs incurred to maintain the FCC licenses are recorded in operating expenses.</span><br/><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_ab012fabd048397f'"><ix:exclude><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; z-index: 100;">10</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></ix:exclude></div></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation></div></div><div class="Section_14"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'1bd-2e8-812-21f-79d2'"><ix:continuation id="c4f3105125d63dc51d72" continuedAt="c3df4581beb88baf2e88"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'1ae-c04-341-035-f4ec'"><ix:continuation id="c7b7de706d59ca1b592c"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">NextNav assesses indefinite-lived intangible assets for potential impairment annually as of October 1 or during the year if an event or other circumstance indicates that NextNav may not be able to recover the carrying amount of the asset. In evaluating indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment, NextNav first assesses qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of the asset is less than its carrying amount. If NextNav concludes that it is not more likely than not that the fair value of the asset is less than its carrying value, then no further testing is required. However, if NextNav concludes that it is more likely than not that the fair value of the asset is less than its carrying value, then NextNav performs a</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">two-step impairment test to identify potential impairment and measures the amount of impairment it will recognize, if any.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'2b4-04f-48e-d97-1eaf'; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Goodwill</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the net tangible and intangible assets acquired in a business combination. Goodwill is not amortized but is tested for impairment annually in the fourth quarter or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate that the asset may be impaired. The Company operates as</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cefc67937aab4a9ab3f6'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="D20260331" unitRef="Number" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="Tag461">one</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">reporting unit. When testing goodwill for impairment, the Company may first perform an optional qualitative assessment. If the Company determines it is not more likely than not the reporting unit&#8217;s fair value is less than its carrying value, then no further analysis is necessary. If the Company determines that it is more likely than not that the fair value of its reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, then the quantitative impairment test will be performed. Under the quantitative impairment test, if the carrying amount of the Company&#8217;s reporting unit exceeds its fair value, the Company will recognize an impairment loss in an amount equal to that excess but limited to the total amount of goodwill.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">carrying value of long-term debt in the Company&#8217;s Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets generally consists of principal amount of debt, net of debt discounts. The Company evaluates its debt agreements to determine whether debt contains embedded features requiring</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">bifurcation</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">from the debt host in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification 815,</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Derivatives and Hedging</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">("ASC 815").</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">If an embedded feature requires</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">bifurcation</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">from its debt host, the Company will account for it as a derivative at fair value. If a hybrid instrument has multiple embedded derivatives requiring bifurcation, the Company will bifurcate a single compound derivative. The Company uses valuation models to estimate the fair value of the bifurcated embedded derivatives. Debt discounts recognized as a result of allocating proceeds to bifurcated embedded derivatives as well as accounting for direct debt issuance costs are amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:11pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The fair value of bifurcated derivatives is presented in the same line item as debt in the Company's Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:11pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Unamortized debt discounts are written off and included in the Company&#8217;s gain or loss calculations to the extent the Company extinguishes debt prior to the original maturity.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-family:Arial; font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'ceccf8c45203d1d7198c'"><ix:exclude><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_c925abb12d761c6456bc'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation></div></div><div class="Section_15"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'1bd-2e8-812-21f-79d2'"><ix:continuation id="c3df4581beb88baf2e88"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cdc2bbbd0ca35216c2d8'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionsAndTranslationsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag641"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Foreign Currency Translation</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The functional currency of NextNav&#8217;s foreign subsidiaries is generally the local currency. Assets and liabilities are translated into U.S. dollars at the exchange rate in effect at the Condensed Consolidated</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Balance Sheet date. Operating accounts are translated at an average rate of exchange for the respective accounting periods. Translation adjustments resulting from the process of translating foreign currency financial statements into U.S. dollars are reported as a component of accumulated other comprehensive loss. Transaction gains and losses reflected in the functional currencies are charged to income or expense at the time of the transaction.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Net transaction gains (losses) from foreign currency contracts recorded in the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Loss were immaterial for the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'639-2f4-8ea-d9d-1cdf'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Quarter_and_YTD_P6'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">three months ended March 31, 2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">and </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c00cb6d6f695dc9b2520'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous Year_P10'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">2025</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">. The only component of other comprehensive loss is currency translation adjustments for all periods presented. No income tax expense was allocated to the currency translation adjustments.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c9d654106680748dfb51'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag642"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:10pt; line-height:14.4pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">Segments</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">NextNav operates as </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cfb998110029e887fc22'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'"><ix:nonFraction name="nn:NumberOfSegment" contextRef="I20260331" unitRef="Number" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="Tag463">one</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'"> operating segment. Equity Method Investment</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:6pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">The Company has an investment in MetCom Inc., a privately-owned Japanese joint stock company (kabushiki kaisha) (&#8220;MetCom&#8221;). The Company provides licenses to its technology, infrastructure and subscriber equipment to MetCom to support MetCom&#8217;s efforts in commercializing terrestrial positioning technology (both TerraPoiNT and Pinnacle) in Japan. Our </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c5f-78f-ebd-b17-6977'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous Year_P26'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; background-color:#ffffff; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">2025</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; background-color:#ffffff"> Form 10-K includes additional information about our significant accounting policies, practices, and the transactions that underlie our financial results, as well as a detailed discussion of the most significant risks and uncertainties associated with our financial condition and operating results.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; background-color:#ffffff">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic; background-color:#ffffff">In addition to historical financial information, some of the information contained in the following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. Forward-looking statements reflect management&#8217;s current expectations and are inherently uncertain. Actual results and outcomes could differ materially for a variety of reasons. You should review &#8220;Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements&#8221; at the beginning of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, as well as Item 1A, &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; in our 2025 Form 10-K, as well as those otherwise described or updated from time to time in our other filings with the SEC, for a discussion of important factors that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results described in or implied by the forward-looking statements contained in the following discussion and analysis. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; background-color:#ffffff">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; background-color:#ffffff">Overview</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; background-color:#ffffff">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">We are the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">market leader in delivering resilient, next generation, complementary positioning, navigation and timing (&#8220;PNT&#8221;) solutions designed to overcome the limitations and vulnerabilities of existing space-based Global Navigation Satellite Systems (&#8220;GNSS&#8221;), including the Global Positioning System (&#8220;GPS&#8221;).</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt"> PNT services are used in nearly every facet of our economy. Cellular and electrical distribution systems depend on GPS-based timing, and the mobile app economy relies on location to create innovative services and to drive data and advertising revenue.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">Public safety and enhanced 911 (&#8220;E911&#8221;) save lives every day with the use of location services.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">GPS has powered the global economy for nearly 40 years. Without high-precision timing from GPS, cellular systems would fail, the distribution of electricity would be impacted, and other aspects of everyday life would be adversely affected.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">Recent international events have demonstrated that having viable systems to backup and complement GPS is a national security issue. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our PNT solutions address these needs and issues in several ways.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">Our technology consists of a ground-based transmitter network operating on low-band spectrum assets in a manner similar to the function of GPS satellites.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">Unlike satellites, our network signals are designed to be much stronger and extremely difficult to jam or spoof.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">In addition, because the signals are terrestrial and low-band, they can penetrate buildings.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">As a result, our technology can act as a complement to satellite-based GPS, especially in urban canyons or deep indoors, and as a backup in case traditional GPS fails due to jamming, spoofing, technical failures, solar flares or other risks to satellite-based services.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">In addition, our location-based services are three-dimensional. Our core Pinnacle technology uses barometric sensors in smartphones and other communications devices and a network of sensors to determine vertical, or &#8220;z-axis&#8221;, location.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">This technology can provide accurate vertical location data to assist first responders, dispatchers and others, or could be used for autonomous systems, such as drones, in need of precise 3D mapping in urban areas, among other uses. </span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our complementary PNT solutions are built on our asset base of FCC licenses that cover 12 MHz of low-band spectrum available for use.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">This spectrum consists of a contiguous</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">8</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz block of</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">900 MHz spectrum covering over</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">90% of the U.S. population and an additional</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">4</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz of complementary spectrum</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">covering part of the U.S. population that was transferred to us in 2025 as a result of a transaction with Telesaurus and Skybridge Spectrum Foundation. That transaction also gave us potential rights to an additional 2 MHz of related spectrum covered by terminated Skybridge Spectrum Foundation licenses.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">These licenses are subject to a Skybridge and Telesaurus petition for reconsideration seeking reinstatement of these licenses. For more information, refer to Note 5 to our condensed consolidated financial statements for the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'0b5-f26-7d2-e89-fa36'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Quarter_P25'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">three months ended March 31, 2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"> included in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">We are evolving our PNT solutions to use 5G New Radio (&#8220;5G NR&#8221;) positioning reference signals (&#8220;PRS&#8221;), under the 3GPP global standard, to determine location and timing - a platform we refer to as NextGen.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">We believe the evolution of our existing technologies and services to a 5G NR PRS capability will improve the efficiency, flexibility, and scale of our operations. 5G NR technologies drive enhanced network performance, capacity, and efficiency across multiple industry verticals. 5G NR enables low-latency, high-throughput connectivity and also improves spectral efficiency, which allows operators to increase returns on investment in licensed spectrum and, with respect to our technology, to improve both the density and availability of PNT signals. 5G NR can also support many different applications, including ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), and massive machine-type communications (mMTC). These capabilities permit 5G NR to support high-performance broadband services as well as emerging use cases in autonomous systems, industrial automation, and the Internet of Things (IoT).</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">As a result, spectrum that can support 5G technologies and services is important to broadband providers and their customers. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">To enable our evolution to 5G NR, we have filed a Petition for Rulemaking (the &#8220;Petition&#8221;) asking the FCC to optimize the Lower 900 MHz radio spectrum band to enable 5G NR operations, the delivery of</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">PNT via a 5G broadband network and in turn support such 5G technologies and services.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">Our Petition requests the FCC allow us to use a single, nationwide 15 MHz spectrum configuration for both PNT and 5G broadband.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">The Petition is subject to an ongoing FCC regulatory review process, and was referenced in the FCC&#8217;s March 27, 2025 PNT Notice of Inquiry.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">Under our proposal, the FCC would</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">create a 5</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz uplink and 10</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz downlink</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">suitable for 5G operations.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">We believe</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">modernizing the Lower&#8239;900&#8239;MHz band will simultaneously enable a high-quality terrestrial PNT network to complement and back up GPS, addressing</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">a critical</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">national security vulnerability, and</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">add&#8239;5G broadband capacity.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">As such, our NextGen capability is being designed with the goal of enabling one or more</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">mobile network</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">operators or other partners to integrate this optimized Lower 900 MHz spectrum into their</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5G network</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">deployments. We expect that these partnerships</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">would</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">result in wide-scale availability of our complementary PNT services and, for our potential partners,</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">additional</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5G broadband capacity.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_6125dbe18492a15f'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">23</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_27"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The backbone of wireless data services, electromagnetic spectrum, is a finite resource.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Our spectrum licenses, which lie in the Lower</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">900</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz band, are referred to as &#8220;low-band spectrum.&#8221;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">There is a finite amount of low-band spectrum available, and</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">low-band spectrum has favorable coverage characteristics compared to higher frequencies, including the ability to provide services indoors and over greater distances.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">These characteristics result in its ability to be used for coverage and to be deployed more economically, with higher-frequency spectrum often used to provide additional capacity in targeted locations.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">The transition to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5G NR for our PNT services will provide a technical capability to support broadband data services, which, subject to appropriate regulatory approvals, would allow the spectrum to be used to help meet the continued, growing demand for wireless data capacity. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">A core element of our strategy is to pursue such partnerships to offset the costs of deploying and operating a widescale, terrestrial PNT network that can act as a complement and backup to GPS. While GPS is fully supported by the U.S. government, we believe it is unlikely that the U.S. government would subsidize an extensive, standalone terrestrial PNT network and other revenue-generating opportunities are limited, given existing use of GPS. However, there is a financially viable path to a widescale terrestrial PNT network that meets critical national security needs through the spectrum optimization proposed by our Petition that would allow it to be used for 5G.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic">Macroeconomic Factors</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">Macroeconomic conditions, including changes in overall economic growth and broader business and government spending priorities, could affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. While our business is not highly sensitive to changes in interest rates, inflation or general capital market conditions, adverse macroeconomic developments may reduce or delay spending by wireless carriers, public sector and other commercial customers for our terrestrial PNT services and may affect the timing of planned projects and deployments. In addition, broader economic uncertainty, including the potential for federal government shutdowns, could delay administrative and regulatory actions by governmental agencies, including the Federal Communications Commission, that are important to the commercialization and expansion of our services. We continue to monitor macroeconomic developments and adjust our execution timelines as appropriate; however, prolonged or worsening economic conditions could negatively affect the timing of our initiatives and the pace of adoption of our solutions.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold">Key Components of Results of Operations</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic">Revenue</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We have generated limited revenue since our inception. We derive our revenue from PNT products and services. Our revenue includes revenue generated through services contracts with wireless carriers, services with applications developers, technology demonstration, assessment and support contracts with government customers, sales of equipment, and licensing of proprietary technology. We recognize revenue when an arrangement exists, services, equipment or access to licensed technology are delivered, the transaction price is determined, the arrangement has commercial substance, and collection of consideration is probable.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic">Operating Expense</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-left:27pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:-4.5pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Cost of Goods Sold</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Cost of goods sold (&#8220;COGS&#8221;) consist of personnel-related expenses, including salaries, benefits and stock-based compensation, and allocated facility costs for our operations and manufacturing teams. COGS also includes expenses for site leases, cost of equipment, software license costs, including cloud hosting costs, and professional services related to the maintenance of the equipment at each leased site. Our COGS may fluctuate from period to period based on changes in operating scale.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Research and Development</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Research and development expenses consist of personnel-related expenses, including salaries, benefits and stock-based compensation, and allocated facility costs for our research and development functions. Research and development costs also include outside professional services for software and hardware development, and software license costs, including cloud hosting costs. We expect our research and development costs to increase for the foreseeable future as we continue to invest in research and development for our current and future products, including our NextGen platform.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_c3f40be1c35413be6186'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">24</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_28"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Selling, General and Administrative</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Selling, general and administrative expenses consist of personnel-related expenses, including salaries, benefits and stock-based compensation, and allocated facility costs for our business development, marketing, corporate, executive, finance, legal, human resources, IT and other administrative functions. Selling, general and administrative expenses also include expenses for outside professional services, including legal, auditing and accounting services, recruitment expenses, travel expenses and certain non-income taxes, insurance and other administrative expenses.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We expect our selling, general and administrative expenses to increase for the foreseeable future with the growth of our business, in pursuit of regulatory and technology initiatives, and as a result of operating as a public company, including compliance with the rules and regulations of the SEC, legal, audit, and additional insurance expenses, investor relations activities, and other administrative and professional services.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Interest Income (Expense)</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:18pt; text-align:justify; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our ability to sell Pinnacle z-axis service may be limited and depends on third-party adoption and market demand.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We do not sell our Pinnacle z-axis solutions directly to end users. Instead, we provide location technology that integrates with devices and applications that are created or distributed by third parties. Accordingly, our future growth significantly depends on third parties choosing to incorporate our technology into smartphone devices, applications and other new device types and markets that utilize location. We also depend on our customers, resellers and licensees to develop products and services with value-added features to drive sales and demand. Because GPS has been viewed in the marketplace as a reliable geolocation service provided for free to end users, our customers may not see a business need to integrate our solutions into our devices and applications. Despite efforts to educate customers about the need for z-axis geolocation services, there can be no assurance that such efforts will be successful and as a result, a market for our solutions may not be created or result in meaningful revenue.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">The majority of our business plan depends on selling services that must be licensed and integrated into our customers&#8217; platforms for sales to end users, and we typically only generate revenue from the arrangements when end users access those third-party platforms and utilize our services.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our business plans are dependent in part on the sale of location services to our customers, which are third-party developers who use our services to create applications for use in mobile devices, on vehicles and in other platforms. For these types of contracts, we recognize revenue when end users access and use our customers&#8217; applications.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">As a result, our business plans are also dependent in part on the success of our customers in selling their own products and services to end users. Contracts of this type do not contain purchase commitments and our limited operating history makes estimating the future variable volume and revenue associated with these contracts difficult. If our customers take longer than expected to integrate our services into their applications or are unable to sell their applications in the volumes or timeframes we expect, then the use of our services by end users and the related recognition of revenue could be delayed or may never occur.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">We may</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">not be successful in the evolution of our operations to</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">utilize 5G NR signals, which will increase our costs and may increase the challenge of adopting our services, and the time it takes us to evolve our service may differ from our estimates.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We are currently evolving our core technology from one reliant on a transmission that was designed to be technically compatible with GPS and GNSS receivers to one that is being designed to be technically compatible with the 5G NR ecosystem. This carries risks related to the technical performance of this transmission and the availability of equipment in the 5G NR ecosystem compatible with our spectrum and operations. If the technical performance of the 5G NR transmission is not similar to the technical performance of our legacy technologies, then the market for our services may be diminished.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">We must also secure approval from the FCC for this modified use of our licensed spectrum. We have submitted a petition to the FCC seeking this authority, which has been opposed by certain other users in the lower 900 MHz band. The petition remains pending before the FCC. Further, while we intend our signal to be compatible with the 5G NR ecosystem, we may not be successful at integrating our service into commercial 5G NR transmitters, core network, receivers or other system components, which would significantly reduce the market for our services.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">If there are significant delays in our evolution to 5G NR-compatible technologies, including technology,</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">ecosystem, standardization or other delays, our ability to offer our services to customers including the U.S. Federal Government and commercial entities will be impacted. If any or all such delays occur, our business may be harmed.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_1564f567a6680a5c'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">33</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_37"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our NextGen business strategy is dependent on entering into partnerships with third-party wireless operators; failure to secure these partnerships could prevent us from deploying our 5G services.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our NextGen technology plans are</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">largely dependent</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">upon our ability to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">enter into</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">strategic partnerships with wireless operators to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">utilize</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">our spectrum licenses for 5G broadband services in the manner</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">set forth in</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">our petition before the Federal Communications Commission ("FCC"). The process of negotiating and securing these partnerships is complex, time-consuming, and subject to factors beyond our control, including the strategic priorities of potential partners, competitive bidding for spectrum usage, and general economic conditions.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Even if we are successful with our FCC petition, there is no guarantee that wireless operators will be willing to partner with us on commercially reasonable terms, or at all. If we are unsuccessful in entering into such partnerships, we may be unable to deploy or</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">operate</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">our 5G</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">PNT</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">services. Furthermore, any inability</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">to execute</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">these partnerships could significantly diminish the value of our spectrum assets and impair our ability to generate revenue or achieve profitability. Any failure or significant delay in establishing these relationships could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and the long-term viability of our NextGen service.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">We face intense competition in our market, especially from competitors that offer their location services for free, which could make it difficult for us to acquire and retain customers and end users.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The market for development, distribution and sale of location services is highly competitive. Many of our competitors have strong name recognition, sizable customer bases and significantly greater financial, technical, marketing, public relations, sales, distribution and other resources than we do. These competitors often offer competing services for free and have the financial capabilities to continue to improve upon their location services offering without charging a fee. Certain of our competitors are already vying for market share in the 3D location space through their participation in a federal regulatory proceeding involving the FCC in which wireless carriers are being required to enter into relationships with 3D location vendors in order to enable accurate 3D location information to be conveyed to E911 emergency dispatchers with each wireless call made to E911 emergency services. Although we believe our services currently offer an improved functionality over the services offered for free, there is no certainty that we will be able to achieve broad market appeal for our 3D location services.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">In addition, there is no guarantee that our services will be as reliable and with the same geographic coverage as the currently available geolocation services, which may impact our ability to attract new or retain existing customers to utilize our products over the free services offered by our competitors. The performance of our services may vary based on ambient conditions, both physical and environmental, which may impact the timing and location accuracy of the system. If our services are not meaningfully superior to those available at lower or no cost, we may have difficulty selling our services, achieving widespread adoption of our services and our business, financial position and results of operations may be harmed. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">We face competition from multiple sources.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our services compete against: (i) other satellite and terrestrial based location technology offerings, such as GPS, Observed Time Difference of Arrival and terrestrial beacons; (ii) other providers of Wi-Fi and cell-based positioning, such as Google, Apple and Polaris; (iii) venue-based solutions such as Bluetooth Low Energy; and (iv) other proprietary location solutions. In the smartphone location provider market, because Apple and Google control a large percentage of the market share for smartphone operating systems, already provide their services on a nationwide basis, and offer location provider services free as part of the iOS and Android markets, we are constrained in the distribution and monetization of our services in that market. As noted above, those vendors that secure access to wireless handsets for their 3D location services may be able to leverage a significant competitive advantage over other location service vendors. There are also a number of new location technologies in development that may further increase competition to support location capabilities in various wireless devices (such as Internet of Things) and which may require us to meet more stringent accuracy standards.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:8pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Certain of our competitors are substantially larger than us and have greater financial, technical, marketing and other resources. Thus, many of these large enterprises are in a better position to withstand any significant reduction in spending by customers in its markets, and often have broader product lines and market focus, have greater brand recognition and may not be as susceptible to downturns in a single market. These competitors may also be able to bundle their products together (such as with mapping software) to meet the needs of a particular customer, may be able to respond more rapidly to new or emerging technologies or changes in customer requirements and may be capable of delivering more complete solutions than we are able to provide. If large enterprises that currently do not compete directly with us choose to enter our markets by acquisition or otherwise, competition for both revenue and data would likely intensify. In addition, the growth of new location technologies currently in development may further increase competition to provide these new technologies. If we are not able to compete successfully for customers, our financial position may be materially adversely affected.</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_ed03d4193838ad01'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">34</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_38"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our Pinnacle network infrastructure is dependent on a hosting arrangement with AT&amp;T.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We entered into an equipment hosting agreement with AT&amp;T, expiring</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">in October</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">2028</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">(subject to earlier termination after three years in certain circumstances), and there is no assurance that the agreement will be renewed. We have no contractual right to require AT&amp;T to continue its relationship with us beyond the existing term of the equipment hosting agreement and AT&amp;T may elect not to renew our contracts or we and AT&amp;T may not be able to come to an agreement on renewal or extension terms at or before the end of agreement term. These adverse effects could include, without limitation, us having to abandon, alter and/or delay the deployment of products, services or processes that rely on such intellectual property; having to procure and pay for licenses from the holders of intellectual property rights that we seek to use; and having to pay damages, fines, court costs and attorney&#8217;s fees in connection with intellectual property litigation.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_873632b746f37943'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">39</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_43"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our results could be adversely impacted by increased inflation and supply chain pressure impacting our or our vendors&#8217; expenses and availability of resources and components.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Inflation and inflationary pressures have impacted, and may continue to impact, our business</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">and the businesses of our suppliers and vendors. line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our business and strategy depends on access to radio spectrum to provide our location services, and optimized access to such spectrum is not a certainty.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">Through our wholly owned affiliate, Progeny LMS, LLC, we hold 354 licenses issued by the FCC to use radio spectrum for location services within the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">902-928</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz band, identified by the FCC as the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span a third party in</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">2025.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">When the FCC created the M-LMS service, it used an auction</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">process to issue three M-LMS licenses in each of 176 Economic Areas (&#8220;EAs&#8221;) in the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">U.S. Progeny&#8217;s 354 M-LMS licenses</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">provide coverage of most of the U.S. and</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">the vast majority of</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">populated areas within the U.S., but the amount of spectrum authorized by its licenses varies by location.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Progeny holds all three M-LMS licenses authorizing the use of 12 megahertz of spectrum in 81 EAs, it holds two M-LMS licenses authorizing the use of 8 megahertz of spectrum in another 32 EAs, and it holds one M-LMS license authorizing the use of 4 megahertz of spectrum in another 47 EAs.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">The remaining M-LMS licenses are all held by the FCC in reserve.</span><span
