style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">Progeny&#8217;s M-LMS spectrum licenses are subject to rules that were adopted by the FCC more than</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">thirty</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">years ago and do not reflect (and are often incompatible with) current technology in the fields of radio signal modulation (such as</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5G transmissions) and wireless PNT services. Certain of our location services depend on our ability to use portions of the radio spectrum licensed by the&#8239;FCC in a manner that is inconsistent with the rules applicable to M-LMS services in this spectrum. We have therefore filed a petition with the FCC seeking to update the rules and</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">optimize</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">902-928</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz spectrum</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">band to enable 5G operations. Our petition has been opposed by third parties that use portions of the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">902-928</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">MHz band for other purposes, many of them on a secondary, subordinate basis to our licensed operations. We continue to work with the FCC and interested third parties in seeking approval for our</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Petition</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">so we can deploy next-generation PNT services using</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">state-of-the-art</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5G technology in that band.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">The FCC has initiated interagency review of a draft notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to promote the development of positioning, navigation, and timing technologies and solutions. Such FCC action is subject to interagency review and coordination with other federal entities, including those responsible for national security, public safety, spectrum management, and other governmental interests. The interagency review process can be unpredictable and there is no assurance that the NPRM will be consistent with our petition or that FCC will adopt the NPRM, issue a report and order, or do so within a timeframe, scope, or structure that supports our business objectives.</span></p><p style="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:14pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">The FCC regulatory process is subject to other legal, technical, political, and policy considerations beyond our control. Our petition continues to face opposition from third parties who may seek to delay, modify, or prevent FCC action through the regulatory process or by advocating for legislative or executive branch actions that could stall, condition, or halt FCC consideration of matters relevant to our strategy. For example, the U.S. House Committee on Appropriations recently approved an amendment to federal budget legislation that, if signed into law, would affect the FCC&#8217;s authority, discretion, or resources to take certain regulatory actions, including actions related to spectrum policy and rulemaking processes on which our plans depend. Such legislative action may be modified, rejected, time&#8209;limited, or enacted, and its outcome and impact remains uncertain.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">Any of these factors could result in the FCC not issuing an NPRM, not adopting a report and order or adopting rules that do not permit the optimization or use of the lower 900 MHz band on terms that are commercially practicable for us. </span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">If we are unable to obtain the necessary FCC approvals on a timely basis, or at all, our ability to execute our business strategy, deploy planned services, attract partners or customers, and generate anticipated revenues would be materially and adversely affected and could result in a significant decline in the market price of our common stock. </span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt; background-color:#ffffff"><span style="font-size:10pt">In addition, if the FCC does reconfigure the spectrum, it may decide to use an auction as part of the process of distributing the spectrum licenses it holds in reserve. We may be required to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">participate and compete with other bidders in such an auction, with no certainty of winning. If we are unable to secure additional M-LMS licenses or suitable alternative spectrum in a different frequency band, our ability to expand certain of our services nationwide may be negatively impacted, which may have a negative impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#8239;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt"> </span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_6659a15b2a8d112e'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">42</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_46"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">If we are able to convert our signal transmissions to a</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">G NR platform, the FCC may not permit us to realize all of the benefits of our</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">5</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">G NR architecture, including the additional</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">transmission of high-throughput non-PNT-related voice and data alongside our PNT data.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">One</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">of the significant benefits of converting our spectrum transmissions to a 5G NR platform would be a substantial increase in the data transmission capacity of our network, thus facilitating the carriage of non-PNT-related two-way voice and data services alongside our core PNT data transmission. The FCC&#8217;s rules already permit us to use our currently licensed LMS spectrum for the carriage of two-way voice and data services, but these communications must be related to our PNT services and are not permitted to be interconnected in real time with the public switched network unless a store and forward technology is used. Therefore, to maximize the benefit of a conversion to a 5G NR platform, assuming the conversion is successful, we</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">have requested flexibility from the FCC permitting us to use our spectrum for additional non-PNT-related services in addition to our PNT offerings.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt"> Our proposal has faced substantial opposition from other users of the 902-928 MHz band, and there is no certainty that the FCC will provide us this flexibility nor is there certainty with respect to the extent of the flexibility that is provided. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our FCC licenses authorize the use of radio frequencies that are shared with other radio services, which could result in harmful interference and impairment to our use of our licensed spectrum.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our LMS licenses authorize us to use portions of the 902-928 MHz band. This is a shared frequency band that is used for a number of purposes both by individuals, businesses and the federal government. Other services that are authorized to use these frequencies include federal radiolocation systems; industrial, scientific and medical devices; licensed amateur radio operations; and certain unlicensed devices. Our use of the spectrum is subject to FCC requirements that our operations must accept interference from other uses of the spectrum that have more senior rights to the spectrum. We have been successful thus far in using our LMS spectrum to operate location services without experiencing material impairment of our location services caused by more senior spectrum uses, but no certainty exists that we will be able to continue to do so with either the current-generation systems or following our proposed transition to a 5G NR platform. More</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">senior uses of the 902-928 MHz band could become more numerous or could alter the characteristics of their transmissions in ways that could increase the interference to our location services, resulting in diminished coverage, consistency and accuracy of our location services.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">In addition, our licenses</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">are conditioned upon our</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">ability to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">demonstrate</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">through actual field tests</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">that</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">our systems do not cause</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">unacceptable</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">levels of</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">interference to unlicensed</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">devices. The FCC issued a decision in</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">2013</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">that concluded that, based on field tests, we had successfully</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">demonstrated</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">that our location services did not cause unacceptable interference to such unlicensed</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">devices. Third-party challenges to that FCC decision are still pending. Further, changes in our operations could alter the transmission characteristics of our location services, potentially requiring us to provide further demonstrations that our location services do not cause unacceptable</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">levels of</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">interference to those unlicensed</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">devices. No certainty exists that the FCC would conclude in the future that we&#8239;have succeeded in</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">making</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">such a demonstration a second time.&#8239;We have</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">requested</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">that the FCC</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">eliminate this requirement. However, the FCC may decline to change the rule, and if we are unable to make this demonstration to the satisfaction of the FCC, we may not be able to make changes to our operating characteristics, potentially preventing the future implementation of desirable innovations.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our LMS licenses are subject to renewal by the FCC and no certainty exists that we will be able to secure ongoing renewals of our licenses.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><a href="#"></a><span style="font-size:10pt">LMS licenses are issued by the FCC for renewable periods of ten years. Progeny&#8217;s LMS licenses have different renewal deadlines, with the current license term for 33 of them extending until March 9, 2027, 52 of them until July 14, 2029, 78 of them until July 19, 2030, and 43 of them until October 5, 2031.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">For another 148 of our LMS licenses, the most recent term expired on July 19, 2020. We filed timely renewal requests for these LMS licenses at the FCC, which remain pending. The FCC&#8217;s rules do not identify a specific threshold that must be demonstrated in order for us to secure renewal of our LMS licenses, which means the applicable threshold is the FCC&#8217;s statutory obligation to grant a renewal of our licenses if it serves the public interest.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">The FCC has never denied an application that was filed by Progeny for renewal of its LMS licenses and we believe that our most recent license renewal applications satisfied all of the FCC&#8217;s requirements for grant. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Beginning in 2029, however, our LMS license renewal applications will be subject to new FCC rules placing additional conditions on license renewal applications. Specifically, to secure additional renewals of our LMS licenses we will be required to demonstrate compliance with additional requirements, including that we have satisfied its build-out construction requirements, that we use our network to provide service to the public, and that the service provided is at least at the same level of service that was demonstrated at the time of our build-out showing. No certainty exists that we will receive the currently applied for renewal or continue to meet the requirements of such renewal for future applications. If we fail to secure renewals for our LMS licenses, we will not be able to pursue our next-generation PNT services</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">as previously planned and our business, financial condition and results of operations will be materially harmed.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_37d752c8091ac5fd'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">43</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_47"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Many of our LMS licenses are subject to end-of-term build-out requirements maintained by the FCC, and no certainty exists that we will be able to comply with the build-out requirements for all of our licenses.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">226 of Progeny&#8217;s 354 LMS licenses are subject to FCC rules</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">that require licensees to make productive use of their licensed radio spectrum by a specific deadline and</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">generally continue</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">such use throughout the term of the licenses. If a licensee</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">fails to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">satisfy its build-out deadlines, the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">licenses</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">would</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">be</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">terminated, unless it obtains an extension of time to construct or</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">secures</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">a waiver of the requirement.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">With respect to 154 of Progeny&#8217;s 226 LMS licenses that are subject to end-of-term buildout deadlines, Progeny filed notifications with the FCC that the construction of the required networks was completed and operational by the buildout deadline or by an extended deadline that was requested by Progeny.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">On April 17 and 18, 2023, the FCC &#8220;accepted&#8221; (i.e., approved) the build-out showings for 78 of these 154 LMS licenses.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">The buildout showings for another 76 of Progeny&#8217;s LMS licenses remain pending before the FCC. While we do not currently have reason to believe that the FCC will decline to accept these build-out showings, there is no certainty that the FCC will act favorably on these 76 buildout showings.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Finally, with respect to Progeny&#8217;s remaining 72 LMS licenses that are subject to buildout deadlines, Progeny has filed two requests for extension of the applicable buildout deadline, each request seeking an additional two years to complete construction of the required network.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">The 72 LMS licenses covered by these buildout extensions authorize the provision of location services in many of the least populated EAs authorized by Progeny&#8217;s LMS licenses. These extension requests, which remain pending, were based on multiple justifications that have been deemed by the FCC to be sufficient to merit the grant of such extensions in comparable cases involving other FCC licensees, although no certainty exists that the FCC will conclude that Progeny&#8217;s extension requests will be similarly warranted.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160; </span><span style="font-size:10pt">If the FCC declines to accept any of our buildout showings, or declines to grant extensions of the buildout deadlines for those areas where Progeny has not yet completed the construction of its location service network, Progeny will lose access to its licensed spectrum and may be unable to secure alternative spectrum for these locations, preventing us from providing PNT services in these locations, which may have a material adverse impact on our business.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Our retention and use of our LMS licenses has been the subject of ongoing objections by third parties that could result in the revocation or non-renewal of our LMS licenses.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The FCC&#8217;s oversight of radio spectrum is conducted using a largely public process that is generally governed by the Administrative Procedure Act and the FCC&#8217;s rules on public participation in spectrum allocation and licensing proceedings. As a result, our retention and use of our LMS licenses has been the subject of comments and objections from third parties, including other users of the 902-928 MHz frequencies and other current and former licensees of LMS spectrum. In the past, the FCC has regularly rejected and dismissed these objections to our retention and use of our LMS licenses, but no certainty exists that the FCC will continue to do so in the future. Certain of the previous objections remain pending before the FCC, meaning that the FCC could still act on them in a manner that is adverse to us.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">If the FCC acts on any current or future objections by third parties, our LMS licenses could be revoked or not renewed, which will have a material adverse impact on our ability to use the spectrum as</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">previously planned and our business, financial condition and results of operations will be harmed.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">A portion of our business plan targets government customers, which subjects us to risks, including early termination, audits, investigations, sanctions and penalties.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">One of our</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">objectives</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">is to develop business relationships with U.S. government agencies for the provision of our products and services. We currently contract directly with U.S. government agencies, including NASA, and perform as a subcontractor to other contractors under U.S. government programs.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">As a U.S. government contractor, our business</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">is subject to statutes and regulations applicable to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">companies</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">doing business with the U.S. government, including the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or FAR;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">and NASA FAR Supplement, or NFS.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The funding of U.S. government programs is subject to annual U.S. Congressional appropriations. In addition, the U.S. government may modify, curtail or terminate its contracts and subcontracts without prior notice at its convenience and in that event, the counterparty to the contract may generally recover only its incurred or committed costs and settlement expenses and profit on work completed prior to the termination. If the government terminates a contract for default, the defaulting party may be liable for any extra costs incurred by the government in procuring undelivered items from another source, among other potential contract damages. The termination of funding for a U.S. government program that we support, or any modification or curtailment of our U.S. government prime contracts or subcontracts, would result in a loss of anticipated future revenue attributable to that program, which could have an adverse effect on our operations, financial condition or U.S. government customer demand for our products and services.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_5ff1f19b2e2059d4'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">44</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_48"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">In addition, U.S. government contracts normally contain additional requirements that may increase our costs of doing business, reduce our profits, and expose us to liability for failure to comply with these terms and conditions. These requirements include, for example:</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-left:48pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:-24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">comply with</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">public company regulations and manage our operations effectively.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">operate</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">with</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">a very small</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">number of employees, and our success depends on the continued service and performance of this lean team. As a public company, we are subject to complex reporting, legal, and accounting requirements that demand</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">significant time</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">and attention. Because of our limited</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">headcount,</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">our executive officers must personally devote a substantial</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">portion</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">of their time to compliance and SEC reporting tasks. This diverts their attention away from our primary business</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">objectives. Our small staff makes it difficult to</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">maintain</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">an ideal "segregation of duties" within our internal control over financial reporting. This increases the risk that errors or fraud could occur and not be detected in</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">a timely</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">manner.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">The loss of even one or two employees could disproportionately disrupt our operations, as we lack the "bench strength" or redundancy found in larger organizations to easily redistribute specialized tasks.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">To meet our public obligations, we rely on outside consultants, auditors, and legal counsel. This increases our operating costs and makes our compliance dependent on the availability and performance of these third-party providers.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:23.75pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">If we are unable to effectively manage our limited human resources or if we fail to scale our staff as our strategy progresses, we may experience delays in our filings, weaknesses in our internal controls, or a failure to execute our business plan, any of which could materially and adversely affect our stock price.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_6e6b5fd2fbdcc9bc'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">48</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_52"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">We have never paid dividends on our capital stock, and we do not anticipate paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:24pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The continued operation and expansion of our business will require substantial funding.
